name: Tree Destruction
description: Given a tree$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ with $$$n$$$ vertices. You can choose two vertices $$$a$$$ and $$$b$$$ once and remove all vertices on the path from $$$a$$$ to $$$b$$$, including the vertices themselves. If you choose $$$a=b$$$, only one vertex will be removed. Your task is to find the maximum number of connected components$$$^{\text{†}}$$$ that can be formed after removing the path from the tree. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$A tree is a connected graph without cycles. $$$^{\text{†}}$$$A connected component is a set of vertices such that there is a path along the edges from any vertex to any other vertex in the set (and it is not possible to reach vertices not belonging to this set)
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the size of the tree. The next $$$n-1$$$ lines contain two integers $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \le u, v \le n$$$, $$$u \ne v$$$) — the vertices connected by an edge. It is guaranteed that the edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ across all test cases does not exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output one integer — the maximum number of connected components that can be achieved using the described operation.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.
